column1: # Named exceptions to scripts/check-canonical-tokens.sh (mika#2201).
# SHIPPED EMPTY, AND MEASURED EMPTY ON 2026-09-20. If this file is non-empty at
# merge time, its contents ARE the measure of the pre-existing defect, and every
# row carries its follow-up ticket.
# FOUR MANDATORY FIELDS, TAB-SEPARATED:
#   fichier   repo-relative path of the accused file
#   jeton     the token or callout key the lint accused
#   ticket    the follow-up ticket that will remove this row
#   date      YYYY-MM-DD the row was added
# A row missing any of the four fails the build. An exception without a ticket
# is a permanent exception wearing a temporary one's clothes.
# SELF-CLEANING, AND THAT IS WHAT SEPARATES THIS FROM A JUNK DRAWER.
# The lint refuses a row whose file no longer carries the accused token. So a
# row reddens ON THE DAY OF THE REPAIR rather than surviving it by months. That
# is the whole defence against § R4: *one token wrongly accused, and the lint
# stops being read* — and its mirror, *one exception that outlives its cause,
# and the list becomes the drawer the real regression hides in*.
# NEVER a broad pattern. One row, one file, one token.
# NOTE — this file has NO counterpart for the exhaustiveness scan. There, the
# doctrine admits no exception: a match site is DECLARED in
# scripts/canonical-tokens.tsv, never allowlisted. A match site nobody wants to
# declare is a match site to delete (mika#2201 § D5/D6).
# fichier
